speech_segments.text: that I learned about twenty-four songs of his. Um. We did fourteen in the picture.

speech_segments.speaker: carradine
speech_segments.text: Um. After all the study, it really turned out all I was really trying to do was find a way to talk.

speech_segments.speaker: carradine
speech_segments.text: Because the story could have been about anybody, you, me, anybody out there. It was, you know, a guy who had a hard time in his youth and went out to try to seek his fortune.

speech_segments.speaker: carradine
speech_segments.text: Wasn't the greatest guy in the world. No, not at all so. But you know, we had a difficult marriage and definitely a difficult life.

speech_segments.speaker: carradine
speech_segments.text: And he had something he stood up for and some things he fell down over. You know, and the movie basically was arguments with his wife, uh, jumping on and off trains, having fights, and uh, singing songs.

speech_segments.speaker: carradine
speech_segments.text: That's really what it was about. The monitoring and all the study, and it definitely helped. But the study was not what was important about it. What was important about it was throwing myself into it.

speech_segments.speaker: host
speech_segments.text: Then how was Ashby? How was Ashby?

speech_segments.speaker: carradine
speech_segments.text: He might be the best director I've ever worked with. I'm not sure. It's either him or Walter Hill, and I can never quite decide.
